Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as background noise can interrupt the flow of the call. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Jennifer Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Robert Kline, Chief Medical Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Strategy Officer; Mark Gonzalez, Chief Information Officer; Emily Wong, Chief Human Resources Officer; and Thomas Reilly, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, with a spotlight on our robust financial performance, the contributions from recent acquisitions, shifts in our acuity mix driving revenue, strong net patient revenue growth both year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, effective management of labor costs, our outlook for operating margins, evolving trends between inpatient and outpatient volumes, and solid increases in total admissions and patient days. These metrics highlight our resilience in a landscape shaped by moderating inflation, labor challenges, and the push toward value-based care and outpatient services.

Our consolidated net revenues reached $2.48 billion, up 7.8% year-over-year, marking our ninth consecutive quarter of organic growth, with same-hospital net patient revenues climbing 6.2% to $2.31 billion on modest volume gains and favorable pricing. Volumes showed steady recovery, particularly in outpatient areas, while profitability strengthened with adjusted EBITDA at $462 million, up 12.4% and expanding margins to 18.6%. Recent bolt-on acquisitions like Southeast Regional Health Partners and Midwest Specialty Care Group have been immediately accretive, adding significant revenue and synergies while enhancing our outpatient mix. Acuity improvements, reflected in a rising case mix index, contributed meaningfully to per-admission revenue, and we're guiding operating margins higher amid disciplined cost controls.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Jennifer to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Jennifer Lee:
Thank you, Michael, and good morning, everyone. As Michael highlighted, we had an exceptionally strong quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.48 billion, an increase of 7.8% compared to the same period last year and 4.3% quarter-over-quarter. This growth was driven by increased patient volume across our 42-hospital network spanning 12 states, favorable payer mix shifts, the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives including AI-powered claims scrubbing that reduced days in accounts receivable to 45 from 49 days, boosting cash collections per adjusted patient day by 5.1% to $2,450, and the meaningful impact of our strategic acquisitions totaling $745 million in enterprise value.

Diving deeper into net patient revenue, which hit $2.48 billion with that 8.7% YoY and 4.3% QoQ gain, volumes led the way: total admissions rose 5.2% YoY to 128,500, including a 7.1% surge in elective inpatient procedures like orthopedics and cardiology interventions such as TAVR and PCI, while outpatient volumes jumped 9.8% YoY, powered by our 65 ambulatory surgery centers now representing 22% of net patient revenue. Adjusted patient days increased 6.4% YoY with average length of stay steady at 4.7 days, and QoQ admissions grew 2.8% with outpatient equivalent visits up 5.1%. Case mix index climbed 3.2% YoY to 1.85, pushing net revenue per admission to $19,300, up 3.4%, supported by commercial and managed care at 52% of revenues, up 150 basis points, Medicare at 38%, and Medicaid at 8%, alongside bad debt improving to 2.1% of gross revenue thanks to enhancements like Epic's RevCycle module and Waystar's denial prevention.

On total admissions and patient days, we achieved 128,450 admissions, up 4.8% YoY from 122,600 and 2.1% QoQ from 125,800, with patient days at 762,300, reflecting 3.9% YoY growth from 734,200 and 1.6% QoQ from 750,500. Elective admissions, 42% of the total, rose 7.2% to 54,200, led by orthopedics up 9.1% to 18,450 and cardiology up 6.8% to 15,300, while medical admissions grew 2.9% to 74,250. ALOS held at 5.94 days, down slightly YoY, with CMI up 1.2% to 1.68, and QoQ gains included surgical volumes up 3.5% and observation stays up 8% to 22,500 days. Regionally, Southeast admissions surged 6.2% YoY to 66,800, Midwest up 3.9% to 32,100, and West Coast up 2.1% to 18,250, bolstered by commercial payer mix at 58%, up 1.5 points, and ICU days up 2.4% to 112,400.

Acuity mix changes were a standout, with system-wide CMI rising 3.2% YoY to 1.58—our third straight sequential gain—driving 45 basis points or $28 million of our net patient revenue expansion, about 12% of the top line, and lifting net revenue per admission 5.8% to $14,200. This stemmed from normalized high-acuity care like complex cardiovascular TAVR and MitraClip, oncology infusions, and cardiology volumes up 7% with segment CMI at 2.12, offset by 4% declines in lower-acuity cases amid tighter prior authorizations. Sunbelt markets, 42% of beds, captured 65% of the benefit, with Florida CMI at 1.65 up 4.1% on 9% ortho growth yielding $22,500 per DRG at 38% commercial mix, while Northeast and Midwest held flatter at 1.48. Initiatives like Epic's acuity forecasting across 85% of acute beds improved ED triaging by 22%, routing 15% more high-acuity to inpatient, partnerships with ACOs like Privia for CHF bundles reducing readmissions 18%, and neuro/trauma expansions with Stryker lifting unit CMI to 2.45 and adding $12 million quarterly.

Our recent acquisitions amplified this momentum. Southeast Regional Health Partners—a 450-bed network with five hospitals and 12 outpatient sites in Florida and Georgia, closed late last year for $425 million—and Midwest Specialty Care Group with three tertiary hospitals and eight ASCs in Ohio and Michigan for $320 million in Q1—contributed $285 million in revenue on a pro forma basis, helping drive 18% YoY consolidated growth to $2.85 billion adjusted, or 22% organic. Southeast posted 12% same-facility growth on Medicaid expansion adding 8% volumes and steady commercial rates at 45%, while Midwest volumes rose 15% QoQ with CMI to 1.92 on ortho and cardiology backlogs. These added margin tailwinds, with Year 1 synergies at $28 million of a $45 million target via Vizient GPO shaving supply costs 450 basis points to 22% of revenue and RCM accelerating DAR to 42 days from 51 for $15 million cash unlock. Southeast boosted post-acute capture to 65% internally, surging observation stays 25% and ASC volumes 32%, while Midwest gained from Medicaid redeterminations adding 6% volumes and value-based ACOs projecting $12 million shared savings in 2025 under MSSP Track 3. Outpatient mix improved to 58% from 49%, with tech migrations to Epic forecasting 10% LOS reductions and nurse productivity up 15%.

Volume trends underscore the industry shift: total patient volumes grew 4.2% YoY, but inpatient admissions of 142,000 fell 2.8% YoY and were flat QoQ—fifth straight quarter of declines—while outpatient encounters hit 2.8 million, up 7.6% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, with procedures surging 9.2% led by ortho 12% and GI 11%. This mirrors CMS data with inpatient down 15% since 2019 and outpatient up 25%, driven by Medicare Advantage over 50% penetration enforcing site-neutral payments. Inpatient net revenue per case was $14,200 down 1% acuity-adjusted versus $1,850 per outpatient encounter up 5%, but outpatient margins reached 28% versus 12% inpatient. Sunbelt outpatient exploded 11% with Florida at 14% on 12 new USPI ASCs at 85% utilization, inpatient dipping just 1.2%; Midwest/Northeast inpatient down 5.1% but outpatient up 5% via FEDs capturing 22% ED volume. Robotic da Vinci across 75% ASCs/HOPDs enabled 40% more outpatient procedures with LOS under 24 hours and OR turnaround up 18%, while ApexConnect telehealth handled 250,000 visits converting 35% to outpatient and Qventus AI filled prime slots 92%.

Turning to profitability, adjusted EBITDA reached a robust $462 million, up 12.4% year-over-year, with margins expanding 140 basis points to 18.6%. Operating expenses were $2.02 billion, representing 81.4% of net revenue, down 90 basis points through disciplined management. Labor costs, our largest item at 52% of expenses, rose just 4.1% YoY despite 5.8% RN wage inflation, as we cut contract labor to 8% of workforce—down 2.8%—saving $28 million via the Apex Talent Pipeline with AI-driven Epic MyWork scheduling and local nursing school partnerships; overall labor hit 55.4% of revenue, improving 210 basis points YoY from 57.5% and flat sequentially at 55.1% same-facility, leveraging 8.2% net patient revenue growth to $2.4 billion, 6.1% admissions, and CMI to 1.68 with worked hours per patient day at 8.42. Supply costs rose 6.2% but yielded $28 million Vizient savings on ortho implants and pharma, aligning with HFMA benchmarks. Depreciation and amortization was $185 million on ASC expansions, capex at 4.2% of revenues.

Regionally, Southeast—14 hospitals in Florida, Georgia, Carolinas—drove 55% of EBITDA growth with 9.5-10.2% revenue expansion to $1.12 billion on Medicare Advantage, migration tailwinds, tourism trauma, and JV ASCs; Midwest 11 facilities grew revenues 5.1-6.8% but margins to 17.2% amid Medicaid redeterminations, countered by $20 million cost-outs and Zoom-Epic telehealth for 25,000 visits adding 4% outpatient; West Coast up 7.5% offsetting Medi-Cal pressures via capitated Molina deals. We've divested two rural hospitals for $180 million, recycling into 22 ASC JVs, and our AI risk tool with Google Cloud cut readmissions 12% saving $15 million in penalties.

Net income attributable to common shareholders was $185 million, or $1.42 per diluted share, up 15%, with adjusted diluted EPS at $1.65 beating consensus by $0.08. Balance sheet strong: net debt to adjusted EBITDA at 2.8x from 3.1x, $1.2 billion liquidity including $450 million revolver, operating cash flow $520 million or 112% of EBITDA funding $120 million repurchases under $500 million authorization and $85 million growth capex on three de novo Sunbelt ASCs. Leverage post-acquisitions at 3.1x leaves $1.2 billion dry powder for Texas and Carolinas tuck-ins.

For guidance, full-year 2024 operating margin—adjusted EBITDA less D&A over net patient revenues—at 13.2%, up 110 basis points from prior year on 4.2% same-facility revenue and 1.9% case-mix supply growth. Q4 same-hospital revenue 5-7%, FY EBITDA $1.85-1.90 billion. Q1 2025 operating margins 13.8-14.5%, up 60-130 basis points sequentially from Q4's 13.4%, on 3-3.5% adjusted admissions, 6-7% outpatient, 15 new USPI ASCs, commercial rates 3-3.5%, VBC at 22% lives, labor growth 3.8% with travelers at 8%, non-labor 2.5% via Vizient 7% pharma savings. Full-year 2025 margins 14.5-15.3% implying $1.2-1.3 billion operating income on $15.8-16.2 billion revenues, EBITDA 22.5-23.5%, enabled by Epic Hyperdrive AI cutting LOS 0.2 days in ortho and denials to 4.1%, $400 million capex for five ASCs two micro-hospitals, 70% hedging, $500 million repurchases. Southeast drives 70% expansion; risks include respiratory season $50-75 million costs, Medicare sequestration, cyber with $80 million invested post-Change Healthcare.

Our fortress balance sheet and 'Outpatient First, Tech-Enabled Scale' strategy, including $250 million Oracle digital transformation yielding 97.8% cash collections, three Q3 ASC acquisitions and five partnerships targeting 25% non-acute revenue by 2026, ACO REACH $45 million YTD savings at 35% lives, 250 new beds, AWS predictive analytics for 5-7% Q4 tailwind, CMS joint bundles compressing ALOS 10%, cross-training 12,000 staff reducing specialty reliance 18%, LeanTaaS iQueue and Nuance Dragon saving 1.2 non-direct hours per patient day, virtual nursing pilots for 3-5% lift, $75 million retention bonuses targeting 92% rate, de-risk acquisitions at 2.8x ROI, two Southeast trauma hospitals at 12x EV/EBITDA—position us for 15% FCF yield by 2026 and top-tier ROIC above 12%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Robert Kline for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Robert Kline:
Thank you, Jennifer. Good morning. We are making significant strides in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our readmissions reduction program has shown remarkable results, with a 12% reduction in rates through AI risk stratification and partnerships like Google Cloud. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform delivering 250,000 visits quarterly, remote patient monitoring programs, and AI-powered diagnostic tools integrated with Epic for acuity forecasting and decision support in high-volume areas like CHF and pneumonia.

Following that, David will provide an update on operational efficiency.

David Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Kline. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-driven scheduling with LeanTaaS iQueue and Epic MyWork, and centralized credentialing, which have resulted in significant cost savings like $28 million in premium labor pay, improved patient flow with 18% faster OR turnaround via robotics, and enhanced staff productivity with HPPD at 8.42 alongside 92% prime-time slot fills.

Next, Lisa will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, David. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network through tuck-in M&A like our recent $745 million deals and $1.2 billion dry powder, developing new partnerships such as USPI for 25 ASCs and Privia ACOs, and investing in innovative technologies like Epic Hyperdrive and da Vinci systems. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key Sunbelt markets, enhance our service offerings in high-acuity lines now 55% of revenue, and diversify our revenue streams toward 65% outpatient by 2027.

After that, Mark will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

Mark Gonzalez:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures including $80 million post-Change Healthcare investments aligning with HHS guidelines, to enhance our cybersecurity posture, ensure compliance with regulatory requirements like HIPAA, and mitigate the risk of data breaches. We are also investing in cloud-based solutions like AWS and Google Cloud for predictive analytics, Oracle Health revenue integrity, and full Epic rollout across 85% of sites for scalability and flexibility.

Following that, Emily will discuss our efforts related to workforce development and employee engagement.

Emily Wong:
Thank you, Mark. We are committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly skilled and engaged workforce. We are implementing several initiatives including the Apex Talent Pipeline with AI scheduling, cross-training certifications for 12,000 staff via MediCore Academy, $75 million retention bonuses tied to 12-month tenure, apprenticeships with community colleges, virtual nursing hubs emulating Cleveland Clinic, and wellness incentives to cap benefits at 22%, all promoting a culture of diversity and inclusion while targeting 92% retention and reducing traveler reliance to 4.2%.

Finally, Thomas will elaborate on our compliance efforts.

Thomas Reilly:
Thank you, Emily. We are dedicated to maintaining the highest standards of ethical conduct and regulatory compliance. We have implemented a comprehensive compliance program including AI denial management reversing $24 million claims, clean claim rates at 98% via RPA, adherence to No Surprises Act, Two-Midnight Rule, IPPS updates, and OPPS reforms, to ensure adherence to all applicable laws and regulations, protect patient privacy under HIPAA, and prevent fraud and abuse amid value-based shifts.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on the specific initiatives you are implementing to improve employee satisfaction and retention?

Emily Wong:
Good morning, Alex. Absolutely. Beyond our financial controls, we're transforming the workforce experience head-on. Key initiatives include the Apex Talent Pipeline retention program with AI-driven scheduling via Epic MyWork and partnerships with local nursing schools to build internal pipelines, reducing contract labor to 8% and saving $28 million in premiums. We've rolled out cross-training for 12,000 clinical staff through our Academy platform, cutting specialty role reliance by 18% and boosting efficiency. Generative AI tools like LeanTaaS for predictive staffing and Nuance Dragon for documentation shave 1.2 hours per patient day in non-direct time, with virtual nursing pilots in Texas and Florida projecting 3-5% margin lift. Our $75 million retention bonus pool rewards 12-month tenure, alongside apprenticeships and wellness programs capping benefits at 22%, driving toward 92% retention amid 16.8% national RN shortages. Employee surveys show satisfaction up 15% in pilot sites, aligning with our 52.8-54.1% regional labor metrics.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
What are your plans for addressing the ongoing challenges related to regulatory compliance and cybersecurity threats?

Thomas Reilly:
Thanks, Maria. Compliance and cyber are foundational. We've fortified with a $80 million post-Change Healthcare investment, including AI-powered claims scrubbing from Change Healthcare and Waystar for 97.8% cash collections and 4.1% denial rates, proprietary denial reversal tools recovering $24 million quarterly, and RPA for 98% clean claims under No Surprises Act scrutiny. Our program covers IPPS 2.7-2.9% updates, OPPS site-neutral caps, Two-Midnight compliance via observation growth, HIPAA privacy via Epic MyChart, and fraud prevention in VBC contracts at 35% lives. Regular audits, staff training, and MSSP Track 3 participation mitigate risks, ensuring we're ahead of HHS guidelines and payer audits like UnitedHealthcare's.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Can you elaborate on the potential impact of your strategic acquisitions on your long-term growth prospects?

Lisa Chen:
Hi David. Our $745 million deals—Southeast Regional and Midwest Specialty—are transformative for growth. They added $285 million revenue immediately, boosted outpatient to 58%, delivered $28 million synergies via Vizient supply scale and RCM DAR cuts to 42 days, and positioned us in Sunbelt demographics with 21% over-65 in Florida capturing 65% post-acute internally. Long-term, they de-risk via hub-and-spoke with 32% ASC surge, VBC upside like $12 million MSSP savings, CMI lifts to 1.92, and tech like Epic migrations for 10% LOS cuts. With leverage at 3.1x and $1.2 billion powder, we're targeting tuck-ins from CHS divestitures at 12x EV/EBITDA, aiming for top-10 bed operator status, 65% outpatient revenue by 2027, and 15% FCF yield, mirroring HCA's multiple expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
How are you leveraging AI to improve diagnostic accuracy?

Dr. Robert Kline:
Good question, Sarah. AI is central to our clinical edge. Our Google Cloud risk stratification tool reduced readmissions 12% and avoided $15 million CMS penalties. Epic's acuity forecasting across 85% beds enhances ED triage by 22%, routing high-acuity correctly. Hyperdrive AI targets LOS reductions like 0.2 days in ortho DRGs via decision support, while Nuance Dragon NLP streamlines documentation. In diagnostics, partnerships with Stryker neurovascular and device firms like Medtronic boost CMI to 2.45 in trauma, and predictive analytics forecast 5-7% volume from seasonal illnesses. Early pilots show 18% fewer CHF readmits via Privia bundles, directly improving accuracy and outcomes in cardiology and oncology.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
